flags: minor: choice B ('years of softened translations') also cues the answer to R036-09 (A) and supports R036-05 (A); the three items cover nearly the same insight
R036-01.notes: P5 says for years the narrator never let the father have the real sentence, which is the turning point. A is not compared in the passage, C is wrong (the teacher is shown as fair), and D is never decided. D is the likeliest trap for readers who expect a resolution.

flags: minor: key D closely paraphrases the next clause ('taking the jolts out of every conversation before they reached the other side'), so this is close to a lookup
R036-02.notes: The examples in P2 soften both the father's words and the clerks'. C fails because the conversations went on. A and B are not supported.

R036-03.notes: 'Something he believes he has already paid for' means he feels owed it, so his manner is blunt and entitled. P2 confirms this: he called the bill 'a theft'. D is a literal-reading trap that few will pick.

flags: minor: P5 states the reason outright ('It was not the sentence I had been given. It was the sentence I would have wanted to hear'), so this is close to a lookup
R036-04.notes: The narrator's draft translation leaves out the criticism. A, B and D have no support in the passage.

flags: minor: overlaps with R036-06, which also asks about the narrator's untested expectation of the father; R036-06 choice D ('the criticism the narrator expected him to resent') partly gives away this answer
R036-05.notes: In P6 the narrator braces 'for the sharpness I had spent years catching', so the narrator assumed a reaction that was never tested. B invents a request from the father. C is a literal trap that some will pick. D is unsupported.

R036-06.notes: 'Instead he laughed... thank you for telling him straight.' He welcomed the criticism. A contradicts 'Instead', B is unsupported, and C contradicts 'he will talk to him'.

flags: minor: C ('responsible for Tomas's being so smart') is somewhat defensible on a surface reading, since 'smart' is in the teacher's remarks. But the father replies right after hearing about the interrupting and arguing, and P1 sets up his own forceful way of speaking, so B is clearly better
R036-07.notes: He sees his own conversational dominance in Tomas. C is the main trap. A and D are unsupported.

R036-08.notes: 'Telling him straight' means telling him directly and honestly, without smoothing. A ('straight away') is the only plausible distractor.

flags: minor: R036-01 choice B states the same idea (softened translations), which cues this answer
R036-09.notes: The father assumes the narrator had always been 'trying to get it right', and the narrator does not reveal the years of softening. Getting this right takes linking the last paragraph to P2 and P5. B, C and D do not fit 'otherwise'.
